confidence_notes: Holistic model estimates from general knowledge; no live listings or booking pages were checked. Restaurant and beer anchors are the firmest. Hostel and hotel rates are volatile and July is peak safari season, so their ranges are wide. Cocktail (about 2.5x beer) and wine (about 3x beer) follow the local beer relationship because direct bar-price knowledge is weak. The FX value comes from search-result text attributed to the RBA exchange-rates overview page; I did not open that page directly.
comparable_city_reasoning: Benchmarked loosely to East African safari-gateway and tourist-hub prices: Moshi (Tanzania) and tourist districts of Nairobi (Kenya). Restaurant prices are set below Nairobi levels, and July lodging is raised for peak dry-season demand. Shilling-to-dollar levels were assumed from general knowledge, not checked live.
